public_rationale: Contemporaneous reports substantiate factual and simple instruction-following failures, including in InstructGPT. They do not establish that absent comprehension caused those failures. Scoring the whole causal claim as supported would silently replace it with the narrower statement that the models sometimes failed.
limitations: The supporting items establish only the behavioral component.
Neither benchmark error rates nor selected examples measure how easily anyone could break every named model.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Newer LLMs still lack genuine comprehension and are therefore still very easy for anyone to break.

statement.excerpt: But they still don’t convey genuine comprehension, and so they are still very easy for Ernie and me (or anyone else who cares to try) to break.
statement.document_title: What does it mean when an AI fails? A Reply to SlateStarCodex’s riff on Gary Marcus

from_speaker: anyone else who cares to try
our_interpretation: The ordinary behavioral reading is that interested users could readily elicit clear factual or commonsense errors from the contemporary models.
The words 'and so' additionally attribute those failures to missing comprehension. Demonstrating errors alone does not establish that explanation.
The historical scope is the continuation of the problems identified on August 22, 2020 through the post date, including the successors discussed in the post.
No numerical failure rate, testing budget, or independent measure of comprehension is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Independent tests show readily reproducible failures in contemporary models, and evidence distinguishes absent comprehension as their cause from alternative explanations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative tests show robust performance against ordinary attempts to elicit these failures, or controlled evidence undermines the proposed explanation that missing comprehension causes them.

evidence.publisher: Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton and Owain Evans / arXiv
evidence.explanation: The benchmark documents substantial factual fallibility in the tested GPT-3-era models. It supports the behavioral component, but measures neither users' effort to discover failures nor their proposed cognitive cause.

The report describes false-premise acceptance and failures under multiple constraints, extending the behavioral evidence to InstructGPT. It also reports improved instruction following and generalization, without establishing whether comprehension is absent.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Reproducible tests of the contemporary models that measure failure-discovery effort, together with controlled evidence connecting those failures to an independently defined deficit in comprehension.
